title: Fixed counts and joint feature bins permit negative or positive mean response similarity in seven selected MICrONS reciprocal pairs
abstract: We tested whether fixed wiring summaries determine the response similarity of two-way connections in one MICrONS mouse. The selected graph has 145 cells, 148 directed connections and seven two-way pairs. We held each cell input and output count and the two-way pair count fixed. We then fixed connected-edge totals in 27 joint bins of movie-response correlation and two opportunity lengths, and in area-layer groups. Integer optimization gave mean correlation endpoints of -0.1349 and 0.6838 for the seven two-way pairs. The observed mean was 0.2752. These controls retained 98.61 percent of the endpoint width under cell counts and the two-way count alone. All six solves had zero reported gap; separate graph checks passed. These are feasible endpoints, not null probabilities or confidence limits. One mouse, coarse controls, selected opportunities and uncertain connection calls limit the result. Code, aggregate evidence and external-data regeneration steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Minimum and maximum mean correlation in exactly seven reciprocal pairs. Each row fixes all controls in the rows above it. The dashed line shows the observed mean. Lines connect feasible endpoints; they do not give probability intervals or show that every intermediate value can occur.
